en.title: Raising Sizes at Per-Item Costs Until All Are Distinct
en.description:
Item i has initial size size[i]; each increase by 1 costs cost[i], and sizes cannot decrease. Make all final sizes pairwise distinct and find the minimum total cost.

This site independently prepared the standard I/O and the solution; bounds supplemented where the source lacks them and corrections to examples are stated explicitly in the specification.
en.input: The first line contains n, the second line contains n sizes, and the third line contains n unit costs. OCR141/142/143 and the supplementary text of the same problem restore the complete original bounds: 1≤n≤200000, 1≤size[i]≤10^9, 1≤cost[i]≤10000.
en.explanation: The minimum for the first example is 7: the item with cost 5 stays at 2, the item with cost 4 stays at 3, the item with cost 2 goes from 2 to 4 for 4, and the item with cost 1 goes from 2 to 5 for 3. The "1+4=7" explanation in the original supplementary text contains an arithmetic error; this site uses the correct process. The answers to the other two examples are 1 and 0.
hints: Sort by original size and assign integer size slots in order. Push every item that can already take the current slot into a heap ordered by unit cost descending and assign the slot to the most expensive one; when the heap is empty, jump to the next original size.
